The retail giant partners with Meta to bring AI-powered shopping to the holiday season

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Black Friday shopping can be exhausting, especially when you're juggling multiple wish lists, comparing prices and trying to stick to a budget. But this year, Walmart is giving shoppers the option to hand some of that work over to AI.

On Tuesday, Walmart announced a partnership with Meta that lets customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta's personal AI agent.

Unlike traditional AI chatbots that recommend products and send you links, Muse can take you through the purchasing process without leaving the conversation. Of course, you'll still have to actually approve the purchase, but it could be helpful when time is of the essence.

And if you're nervous about giving AI access to your credit card, Walmart has built in some safeguards.

Let's say you're looking for a blender but you don't want to spend your entire afternoon comparing models. You can tell Muse what you're looking for, how much you're willing to spend and whether you need it delivered.

Walmart handles the product matching behind the scenes through its new Agent Gateway.

According to the retailer, shoppers will have access to the same prices available on Walmart.com, including Black Friday discounts and applicable membership benefits.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Walmart also says the integration doesn't expose your broader shopping history to third-party agents.

I decided to give this a try (hopefully my husband isn't reading this). I started by simply heading to Muse.ai. From there, I described what I wanted. You can be as descriptive as you want or even vague. I simply gave the prompt, "My husband does a lot of yard work and I'd like to find a gift to help make the job easier." I didn't give a budget (it prompted me "what's your budget?) or any other specific requirements, but you can up front to make shopping even more personal and streamlined. Once you've done that, you're going to want to do the following:

Connect your Walmart account. Muse will direct you to Walmart to sign in before returning you to the conversation.

Set your spending limit. When adding your first product, you'll create a Walmart Agent Profile to manage what the AI is authorized to do.

Complete your purchase. You can check out directly through the conversation with your existing Walmart payment method.Muse showed me a few items before completing the purchase. Rest assured it does pause so you can see the choices. My husband has many of the items on the list already, so that hesitation was appreciated. Since my credit card is already connected to Walmart, this safeguard is important. The last thing I want is to spend hundreds of dollars on yard equipment we already have!

Walmart's regular return policy still applies to purchases made through Muse.

The more specific you are about what you need, the more useful AI shopping could be. If you're looking for someone on your list who is difficult to shop for like a teenage boy, this Muse partnership could be a lifesaver. Here are five prompts worth trying.

"Find me the best Black Friday deal on a 55-inch 4K TV under $300 at Walmart."

"Help me buy Christmas gifts for three kids ages 6, 9 and 12 with a total budget of $150."

"Find five tech gifts under $25 that are currently discounted at Walmart."

"Find the best Black Friday deals on wireless headphones under $100. Prioritize battery life and noise cancellation."

"Help me find stocking stuffers for four people without spending more than $50 total."

I'd recommend including instructions to show you the individual prices and total cost before completing any purchase.

Between shopping lists, crowded stores and seemingly endless Black Friday sales, there's certainly an appeal to having AI take care of some of the legwork.

But I'd still recommend double-checking product specifications, customer reviews and prices at competing retailers before letting an AI agent make a purchase. Just because something is discounted doesn't necessarily mean it's the best deal.

Walmart says it plans to bring its shopping experience to additional AI agents and apps in the future. For now, Muse offers another way to tackle your holiday shopping list without opening dozens of browser tabs.

#3072. Apple has iPads running macOS already, but don’t get too excited

With iPads running the same chips as Macs, many have wished Apple would give us the option of running macOS on them instead of the somewhat clunky iPadOS windowing system. Apple’s previous arguments against converging devices have been somewhat weakened by the launch of the touchscreen MacBook Pro.

A new report says that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either …

As iPad hardware has grown more powerful over the years, the software has struggled to keep up. We saw split-screen capabilities first, with full windowing finally coming to the devices in iPadOS 26 last year.

The UI is still rather clunky compared to macOS, however, leading a significant number of people to wish that Apple simply offered the option of using the more powerful operating system on its tablet devices.

I would be comfortable with 11" and 13" devices running macOS. Actually, I don’t require them to run macOS itself, but I do need them to run macOS apps. I wish the iPad could match a MacBook’s productivity. Running macOS on an iPad seems like a reasonable idea. The MacBook Air is now the better price choice, while those needing a powerhouse will always choose a MacBook Pro or Studio.

Some suggest that running macOS on iPad would reduce Mac sales, but I disagree. I own a nearly full-spec MacBook Pro 16" and expect to keep a machine like that, yet I also purchased a MacBook Air for lighter travel. I would prefer an iPad over the Air, but I cannot choose it because it lacks the apps I require. If it supported them, I would buy the iPad Pro with all accessories, and Apple would gain more revenue from me. I appreciate the concept of owning an iPad, but currently it lacks the value needed to justify paying more for a device that simply does less than a MacBook Air.

In a podcast Q&A, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says that Apple is already doing this internally, but there’s no sign of any plans to make it available outside the company.

Apple has iPads internally running macOS, and they’ve had that for some time. The fact that they have the underlying architecture of Apple Silicon that’s the same on the iPad and the Mac gives them the flexibility in order to test these types of things.

In terms if they’re actually going to do it – would they bring macOS to the iPad itself – at this point I don’t think that’s going to happen anytime soon. I’ve checked into this and there’s no ongoing operating system project right now in terms of a brand new operating system for the iPad – there is no work being done to consumerize macOs on the iPad.

Gurman says Apple seems set to continue to make piecemeal changes over time to bring iPad capabilities closer to those of the Mac but is showing no signs of full convergence.

He reiterated that work on a long-rumored giant-sized folding iPad continues.

The other thing I want to say is that I’m really excited for this potential of Project J312. That is, this giant 19-inch, 20-inch foldable iPad. And it’s basically like a gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside.

However, he says there’s no guarantee it will ever launch, saying the timings have already slipped from 2027 through 2028 to 2029, but both cost and yield issues may still kill the project. If it does launch, it’s expected to cost anywhere from $3,000 to $5,000.

#3071. Why Oracle Stock Slumped Today

There are growing doubts about the balance sheets of weaker players in the hyperscaler market.

By Lee Samaha – Nov 25, 2026 at 3:20PM EST

Oracle (ORCL -5.13%) stock was down by more than 8% at midday today. The slump comes on a day of weakness for AI -related stocks. In a nutshell, there are increasing concerns around the costs of AI enterprises developing frontier AI models and, in turn, their ability to pay AI infrastructure companies like Oracle.

The weakening sentiment is evident in the credit default swap (CDS) pricing on its debt. CDS pricing reflects thre price of insuring against a debt default. It's measured in basis points (bps), whereby 100 basis points equals 1%. So, for example, insuring $1 million in debt with a CDS at 100 bps (1%) would cost $10,000 per year.

In the middle of 2025, the CDS on Oracle's 5-year debt stood at just 35 bps, but it closed out 2025 at 154 bps. But here's the thing. Yesterday it spiked to 360 bps, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence.

To put that number into context, the bond market typically assumes that 40% of a defaulted bond is actually paid out, so the implied annual hazard rate can be calculated by dividing the CDS price by the 60% loss in default. In other words, .036/0.6=.06, or 6% a year.

Over 5 years, the cumulative rate equates to almost 26%. While it's important to note this is just the bond market pricing, there is still a lot of fear in the market over Oracle. Those fears are centered on its soaring capital expenditures to fund its AI build-out, which have turned its cash flow negative.

ORCL Net Total Long Term Debt (Quarterly) data by YCharts

The market is clearly worried about the sustainability of AI investment, and in such conditions it makes sense to focus on stronger players like Alphabet on weakness, rather than chase Oracle stock.

While it's true that you can find good TV deals throughout the year (like on Presidents' Day, Labor Day, etc) the very best TV deals happen in November/December. And I'm not just saying that — I myself waited till November to buy my first OLED TV. (The now old, but still amazing LG C2 if you're wondering).

Simply put, the next few days will see the lowest prices on the TVs that are actually worth buying. If you have a shopping question or just want to let me know what deals you're looking for — or what TV you've already purchased — drop me a note! Now on to the deals....

Holy smokes, this is an amazing deal. The LG C6 is hands-down one of the best OLED TVs of 2026. It offers spectacular OLED performance (including ample brightness) and comes with a full slate of four HDMI 2.1 inputs, Dolby Vision support, and just about every gaming-related feature a dedicated gamer could ask for.

It's on sale at its second-lowest price ever and Best Buy is bundling a free $100 gift card. (By comparison, Amazon has the same price sans gift card). It did hit $1,349 earlier this month, but that freebie gift card makes up for the $50 difference in my opinion.

Buying an OLED TV has been one of the best tech purchases I've ever made. My OLED TV provides images that are sharp and realistic. This is especially true when watching dark, k-dramas like My Mister and Lost (both of which I recommend 100% btw).

If you're looking to buy your first OLED, this is the TV I'd buy.

Let me start by saying that we didn't give the 2026 Roku Select Series TV the best review. Yes, it's very affordable, but my colleague Sean Captain said its generally disappointing and you might be better off with the 2025 Roku Plus Series for $299 (if you can still find stock).

However, my mom has the Select Series TV in her living room and I quite like it. The Roku interface is super easy to navigate and the image quality — while not the best — is decent for the price.

If you want a TV with stunning picture quality that'll be the centerpiece of your living room — I'd say look elsewhere. But if you're not super critical and/or just want a budget TV for the bedroom — it's a solid pick now that it's just $20 shy of its all-time price low.

The TCL Designer Series Picture Frame TV is TCL's take on the Samsung Frame. It's a stylish TV than when turned off, can display artwork so that it blends into your living room. There are several sizes available, with prices starting from just $677.

Drumroll, please.......my favorite Black Friday TV deal this Wednesday (11/25) has got to be the TCL QM7L. Here's why: This TV won a Tom's Guide Editor's Choice Award and it also got the coveted Tom's Guide Award for Best Mini-LED TV of 2026.

It's TCL's first Super Quantum Dot (SQD) TV and it offers better contrast and color than rival Mini-LED TVs. All sizes are selling at an all-time price low right now. You can check out our TCL QM7L review for a full breakdown of the TV.

My colleague Dylan Haas reviews TVs for Tom's Guide. He's tested models like the Samsung S85H, Hisense U6 Pro, and more. He recently picked out the 11 Black Friday TV deals he recommends based on his testing. You can see his picks via the link above or check some of them out below.

The Hisense UR8 is an RGB Mini-LED 4K TV. That's a mouthful, but in a nutshell — RGB LED TVs use an array of ultra-small LEDs arranged in dimmable zones. However, unlike Mini-LEDs — RGB LEDs use red, green and blue LEDs. That results in brighter, purer colors than what we’ve come to expect from even the best TVs.

The UR8 is a Best Buy exclusive — along with many other RGB Mini-LEDs — and in typical Hisense fashion — it's disrupting the market with an insanely low price point. Case in point — this TV debuted at $1,699 and it's already down to $849, an all-time price low.

Ok, folks, here is my last blog update for today and it's a good one! The 48-inch LG B6 OLED TV is a Best Buy exclusive and right now it's selling for just $599. That's an insane price for such an amazing TV.

In our LG B6 OLED review we said it's an excellent TV for the price and it even beats the pricier LG C6 when it comes to SDR color accuracy. You also get some great gaming features, a cool design, and impressive black levels. It's our top pick for value and a sick deal for anyone looking to go OLED this year. Other sizes are also on sale, but sadly the 55-inch model appears out of stock at Amazon and Best Buy.

Make sure to come back on Thanksgiving Day as we highlight more of our favorite Black Friday TV deals!

#3068. SpaceX Sued by 2 States Over Grok’s Sexualized Images of Women and Children

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

People used Grok to generate millions of "spicy mode" images.

Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s company violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.

Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX. Shortly after launching last summer, the tool added a “spicy mode,” which enabled people to generate images and videos showing partial nudity and adult-themed videos. Grok Imagine is integrated into Grok, which is Musk’s AI chatbot.

In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.

Read more: After Rampant AI-Powered Abuse, Grok Doubles Down

Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in a press release that SpaceX misled people into thinking that their images and data would be safe.

“When xAI [now renamed SpaceXSI] allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Jones said. “Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this company accountable.”

Donna Rice Hughes, CEO of child internet safety organization Enough Is Enough, praised Oregon and Virginia for taking action against SpaceX.

“It is abhorrent that women and children are preyed upon in this manner and even more repugnant that xAI’s Grok ‘spicy mode’ has not kept up with bad actors who abuse their terms of service,” Hughes told CNET, adding that Musk’s “team can find ways to prevent criminal misuse of Grok, and at the very least, disable Grok’s ‘spicy mode.'”

Grok Imagine launched on Aug. 5, 2025, and within months, it was used to generate millions of sexualized images, which were posted on the social media platform X, which is also owned by Musk’s SpaceX.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield alleged SpaceX “knowingly designed” Grok Imagine and promoted spicy mode’s lack of safeguards as a feature, not a bug.

“It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material,” Rayfield said in a statement. “The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”

During a 9-day span starting in late December, Grok posted about 3 million sexualized images, according to an analysis from the Center for Countering Digital Hate.

In a statement posted Monday on X, SpaceX said that people using Grok to generate sexualized images and videos violated the platform’s terms of service and worked “aggressively to circumvent our safeguards.” The company said it tightened protections after the misuse and continues to test and adjust them as needed. SpaceX also said it notifies law enforcement authorities “when someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content.”

Earlier this year, several minor Jane Does filed a proposed class action lawsuit against xAI after people used their photos to generate child sexual abuse material using Grok via spicy mode. That case is still ongoing.

In July, a victim’s family also filed suit after photographer Russell Bloodworth in Arkansas allegedly used spicy mode to generate explicit photos of children. xAI went on the offensive, suing Bloodworth and South Carolina man Terry Wayne Harwood, who is also accused of using Grok to generate child sexual abuse material. The company seeks damages for expenses incurred in fighting lawsuits and for reputational harm.

SpaceX and xAI have faced lawsuits for other things aside from illicit image generation. The companies were sued for allegedly sharing sensitive data and for allegedly causing users to be hospitalized for psychosis after harmful chat conversations on Grok.

Monday’s lawsuits against SpaceX are among nearly 400 cases brought against 129 AI companies in the US, according to the AI Lawsuit Tracker. Many Big Tech companies have been sued for allegedly harming the mental health of adults and children. In August, Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by US states alleging the company intentionally designed Instagram and other platforms to be addictive to children.

Companies such as ByteDance — owner of TikTok — Snap, Google and others face more than 2,400 federal lawsuits alleging that their platforms harm the mental health of children.

#3067. iOS 27.3 introduces design changes for these Apple apps

iOS 27.3 includes many new features for Apple’s built-in apps, but it also introduces design changes on the iPhone across Calendar, Safari, Music, and more. Here’s what’s new.

Apple is always iterating on the design of its software. While major overhauls like iOS 26’s Liquid Glass don’t come along often, the company makes smaller design changes all the time via software updates. In iOS 27.3, which will launch to all users next month, Apple has design changes coming to four popular apps: Health, Calendar, Safari, and Music.

The Health app gets the biggest design changes.

As seen above, Health introduces brand new Insights, Longevity, and Browse tabs that replace the previous options and include a variety of fresh UI elements like a top navigation row, personalized prompts and coaching, educational videos, and a lot more.

Apple Calendar’s design updates focus on making key buttons more reachable one-handed.

As the side-by-side above shows, the buttons for search and creating a new event have moved out of the top-right corner and into the bottom of the screen.

Calendar also now shows the year at the top of the screen next to the current month, and has updated the ‘Today’ button to show the current date instead.

Safari introduces an optional new design for tabs: Vertical Tabs. You can enable these inside Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ Safari for a different approach to tabs across iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Here’s an example of vertical tabs on iPhone Duo.

Vertical Tabs won’t be for everyone, but they’ve proven popular in other browsers, so it’s great to see Safari add the option.

Apple Music has a subtle but beautiful design update in iOS 27.3 when viewing lyrics in landscape mode.

Song artwork is now able to break the constraints of a square and blend seamlessly into the scrolling lyrics view. Here are examples from Beta Profiles on X:

New in iOS 27.3 Beta: Animated artwork blends into the Apple Music player in landscape mode, and it looks so good. pic.twitter.com/k8rgSEALGo

This lyrics view was previously available on iPhone Duo, but now it’s coming to all iPhones.

What do you think of iOS 27.3’s design updates in apps? Let us know in the comments.

#3066. Deere (DE) Q4 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Management says the ag cycle bottomed in 2026 as replacement demand builds.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 25, 2026 at 3:23PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Deere (DE +4.44%) reported full-year net income of $4.86 billion and confirmed that Equipment Operations delivered a 12.2% operating margin despite varied market conditions. Management reported that the agricultural equipment cycle reached its trough in 2026, with North America leading a measured recovery driven by replacement demand for an aging machine fleet. The company's fiscal year 2027 outlook anticipates net income between $4.5 billion and $5.25 billion, a range that accounts for a one-time non-cash pension settlement charge and an estimated $300 million net tariff headwind. Management stated that structurally higher margins and diversified earnings across construction, dairy, and livestock markets provided stability during the downturn in large agriculture. The company plans to increase capital investments in technology and automation while maintaining flexible production schedules to calibrate inventory levels based on end-market demand developments.

Operator: Good morning, and welcome to Deere & Company Fourth Quarter Earnings Conference Call. Your lines have been placed on listen only until the question-and-answer session of today's conference. I would now like to turn the call over to Christopher (Chris) Seibert, Director of Investor Relations. Thank you. You may begin.

Christopher (Chris) Seibert: Hello. Welcome, and thank you for joining us on today's call. And a happy early Thanksgiving for those of you celebrating tomorrow. Joining me on the call today are John C. May, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, T. Brent Norwood, Chief Financial Officer, and Dan Pulley, Manager Investor Communications. Today, we'll take a closer look at Deere's fourth quarter earnings and spend some time talking about our end markets and our current outlook for fiscal 2027. After that, we'll respond to your questions. Please note that slides are available to complement the call this morning. They can be accessed on our website at JohnDeere.com/earnings.

First, a reminder, this call is broadcast live on the internet and recorded for future transmission and use by Deere & Company. Any other use, recording, or transmission of any portion of this copyrighted broadcast without the express written consent of Deere is strictly prohibited. Participants in the call, including the Q&A session, agree that their likeness and remarks in all media may be stored and used as part of the earnings call. This call includes forward-looking statements concerning the company's plans and projections for the future that are subject to uncertainties, risks, changes in circumstances, and other factors that are difficult to predict.

Additional information concerning factors that could cause actual results to differ materially is contained in the company's most recent Form 8-K, risk factors in the annual Form 10-K, as updated by reports filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. This call also may include financial measures that are not in conformance with accounting principles generally accepted in the U.S., GAAP. Additional information concerning these measures, including reconciliations to comparable GAAP measures, is included in the release and posted on our website at JohnDeere.com/earnings under Quarterly Earnings and Events. I will now turn the call over to Dan Pulley.

Dan Pulley: Thank you, Chris, and good morning. Deere & Company closed out fiscal 2026 with a strong fourth quarter, delivering 9.3% margins within Equipment Operations. For the full year, operating margins for the Equipment Operations came in at 12.2%, resulting in $4.86 billion of net income. Market conditions varied considerably across our businesses this year. In row crop agriculture, our customers managed through a challenging farm economy, while end markets across construction, compact construction, and Small Ag & Turf remained resilient, supported by healthy project activity and steady product demand. Throughout 2026, teams across our factories, warehouses, and offices executed effectively and managed production changes without disruption in a dynamic global market environment.

At the same time, we continued investing in solutions our customers are putting to work across their farms and job sites to help them lower costs, boost productivity, and improve operating outcomes. Looking ahead to 2027, North America is leading the measured recovery in agriculture, with our Early Order Programs pointing to improving demand as an aged fleet and tight field inventories drive replacement needs. In construction, demand for North American earthmoving equipment remains strong, supported in part by data center investment. We will cover more details later in the call, including what is reflected in our wider guidance ranges. Let us now review the results of fiscal year 2026, beginning on Slide three.

Net sales and revenues were up 4% to $47.7 billion, while net sales for the Equipment Operations were up 6% to $41.3 billion. Net income attributable to Deere & Company was $4.86 billion, or $17.95 per diluted share. Moving now to Slide four and our results for the fourth quarter. Net sales and revenues were down 2% to $12.1 billion, and net sales for the Equipment Operations were down 1% to $10.5 billion. Net income attributable to Deere & Company for the quarter was down 1% to $1.05 billion, or $3.89 per diluted share. Let us now take a closer look at fourth quarter results by segment, beginning with our Production & Precision Ag business on Slide five.

Net sales of $4 billion were down 15% compared to the fourth quarter last year, primarily due to lower shipments. Price realization in the quarter was positive by half a point. Currency translation was also positive by about one point. Operating profit was $406 million, resulting in a 10.1% operating margin for the segment. The year-over-year decrease in operating profit was primarily due to lower shipment volumes and sales mix, partially offset by lower production costs and the effects of foreign currency exchange. Turning to Small Ag & Turf on Slide six. Net sales were up 10% year-over-year, totaling $2.7 billion in the fourth quarter, primarily due to higher shipment volumes and favorable price realization.

Price realization in the quarter was positive by approximately 1.5 Points. Currency translation for the quarter was unfavorable by roughly one point. Operating profit for the quarter increased year-over-year to $233 million, primarily due to higher shipment volumes and sales mix, lower warranty expenses, lower production costs, and favorable price realization. Slide seven details our fiscal year 2027 Ag & Turf industry outlook. For Large Ag in the U.S. and Canada, we expect industry sales to be up 5%-15%. The improvement in crop prices during August and September gave many growers an opportunity to market a portion of their crop at improved profitability.

Used inventories have also continued to decline, particularly for combines, leaving dealers in the market better positioned as we enter 2027. At the same time, crop prices have pulled back from their recent highs, and with input costs elevated, farm margins remain tight, which will likely moderate the pace of industry improvement. Even so, customer orders across our North American Early Order Programs are running up double digits from last year, reflecting resilient replacement demand from an aging fleet as customers look for greater productivity. Small Ag & Turf's diverse end markets continue to provide stability for the business. For 2027, we expect industry sales in the U.S. and Canada to be about flat.

Dairy and livestock fundamentals remain healthy, supported by stable, strong cattle prices. Within the turf equipment industry, high mortgage rates and a soft housing market are limiting growth, but low unemployment and strong household net worth continue to support a stable demand outlook as we enter 2027. In Europe, we expect industry sales to be flat to down 5%. While dairy and livestock fundamentals remain favorable, lower crop yields due to recent drought conditions have pressured grower cash flows. When combined with elevated input costs and tighter lending conditions, these pressures continue to delay investment decisions. As a result, we expect industry conditions to remain subdued through 2027.

Within South America, we expect Ag industry sales to be flat to up 5%, keeping industry volumes near historic lows. Conditions across the region remain challenging, particularly in Brazil, where high interest rates and recent currency volatility continue to weigh on purchasing decisions. Weather is also a key variable this season. Soybean planting is running ahead of last year's pace, but a strong El Niño is adding uncertainty as the crop develops. At the same time, a weaker currency is supporting local cash crop receipts.

We expect the industry backdrop to remain challenging early in the year, but we're monitoring the market closely as a rapidly aging fleet and low field inventory levels could help drive a recovery in demand in the back half of the year. In Asia, we expect industry sales to be roughly flat, with slight gains across most of the region offsetting a moderation in India after a strong 2026. Turning to our segment outlooks, beginning on Slide eight. For fiscal year 2027, we expect Production & Precision Ag net sales to increase 5%-15%. This includes approximately 3 points of price realization, partially offset by 1.5 points of unfavorable currency impact year-over-year.

The wider range balances growing confidence in North America with continued uncertainty in other key regions. We are projecting a full-year operating margin of 12.5%-14.5% for the segment, driven by higher sales volumes in North America and favorable price realization, partially offset by production cost inflation. Next, Slide nine covers Small Ag & Turf outlook. Net sales for fiscal year 2027 are expected to be about flat, including approximately 2.5 points of price realization and about 1 point of unfavorable currency impact. Operating margin for the segment is forecast to be in the range of 12.5%-13.5%, reflecting a narrower sales outlook supported by diversified end markets and favorable price realization, balanced by increased investments to support our growth initiatives.

Moving to Construction & Forestry on Slide 10. Net sales for the fourth quarter were up 12% year-over-year to $3.8 billion, primarily due to higher shipment volumes and favorable price realization. Price realization in the quarter was positive by approximately 4 points. Currency translation for the quarter was roughly flat. Operating profit was slightly down year-over-year at $339 million, resulting in an 8.9% operating margin. The change in operating profit was primarily due to increased production costs and higher SA&G and R&D costs, partially offset by favorable price realization. Slide 11 outlines our 2027 Construction & Forestry industry outlook. In the U.S. and Canada, we expect industry sales for both construction and compact construction to be flat to up 5%.

Elevated infrastructure spending and strong non-residential construction, partly driven by data center projects, continue to support healthy contractor backlogs. At the same time, rental companies are refreshing their fleets as rental rates and utilization improve, and used equipment inventories have tightened. These tailwinds are partly offset by continued softness in residential construction as elevated mortgage rates weigh on housing activity. We are also watching the pace of data center investment closely, as any slowdown could temper the current momentum. Within road building, we expect industry sales to be flat to up 5%, supported globally by infrastructure programs and major projects, most notably in North America. Global forestry markets are expected to be roughly flat.

Industry activity should stabilize after a difficult 2026, but the continuation of a soft housing market will limit improvement. Continuing with C&F, our fiscal year 2027 financial outlook for this segment is provided on Slide 12. We expect fiscal year 2027 net sales to range from flat to up 10%, with approximately 2 points of price realization and 1 point of unfavorable currency impact. We anticipate the segment's operating margin to be between 9.5% and 11.5%, as continued strength within the construction industry reinforces incremental investments to unlock growth. Moving to Financial Services on Slide 13. Worldwide Financial Services net income attributable to Deere & Company was $231 million in the fourth quarter.

The year-over-year decrease was driven by unfavorable financing spreads, the impact of a lower average portfolio, and a higher provision for credit losses. For the full year, Financial Services net income was $885 million. For fiscal year 2027, we expect net income of $900 million. The increase is primarily driven by improved financing spreads and a lower provision for credit losses as customer credit conditions continue to stabilize. Slide 14 concludes with our fiscal year 2027 guidance for net income, effective tax rate, and net operating cash flow. For fiscal year 2027, we expect net income between $4.5 billion and $5.25 billion.

This outlook includes roughly $500 million in higher pension-related impacts compared with last year, most of which relates to an estimated one-time tax-adjusted non-cash pension settlement charge of $250 million-$400 million associated with a voluntary lump sum payment option offered to certain U.S. salaried retirees. At this time, we expect to incur this one-time non-cash charge in the second quarter. Our effective tax rate for fiscal year 2027 is expected to be between 23% and 25%. Lastly, net operating cash flow is projected to be in the range of $4.5 billion-$5.5 billion. This concludes our formal remarks. Before we turn to a few key topics, I would like to ask John and Brent to share some opening remarks.

John C. May: Thanks, Dan. This is John. I want to start by thanking our employees for their focus and dedication this year, our dealers for working with us to manage inventory and support the business, and our customers for the trust they place in John Deere. I am proud of what we accomplished together this past year. Fiscal 2026 brought varied market conditions, with each of our businesses at a different point in the cycle. In Large Ag, farmers are still working through tight margins, increasing input costs, and volatile commodity markets. In Construction, markets kept getting stronger, with infrastructure and rental fleet investments supporting strong order books.

In Small Ag & Turf, a diverse mix of end markets, from dairy and livestock to turf, gave a supportive backdrop for growth. Through it all, our teams kept inventories healthy, stayed focused on the investments that mattered most for our customers, and delivered double-digit margins in every segment. For me, that's what stands out most about this year. It showed the strength of Smart Industrial across our business units. Our strategy is to keep investing and innovating through the cycle. That consistency is what makes our growth ambitions possible. In 2026, we showed that we mean it.

Our structurally higher margins and consistent cash generation gave us the flexibility to keep investing in the business while also pursuing targeted acquisitions. The way our team executed this year leaves us well-positioned for 2027, even as our wider guide ranges reflect a broader set of possible outcomes across the industries we serve. Looking ahead to 2027, I have two important takeaways I want to share with you. First, the Ag Equipment cycle troughed in 2026. The proof points from our Early Order Programs point to North America leading the global recovery. External factors like geopolitical influences on crop input inflation will likely moderate the pace of that recovery in the near term.

Even so, an aged fleet and limited field inventories for new equipment are driving required replacement demand, even as farm economics remain tight. We do see further upside for the year, which is why our sales range is wider. The upside depends on filling out the remainder of our North American order book at the pace similar to our Early Order Programs. The other option that could happen is on a backend-loaded recovery in Brazil, where aging fleet dynamics are building rapidly due to a machine usage intensity that is twice the level of North America. Second, momentum remains very strong in North American earthmoving products.

Much of the demand relies on growth stemming from continued data center investment, so we're closely watching current developments around prospective data center assessments from local communities. We've left enough flexibility in our build schedules to calibrate field inventory levels as needed. Brent, can you expand on the outlook for next year?

T. Brent Norwood: Sure, John. For 2027, we are encouraged by the early improvement we are seeing in the North American Large Ag order books, though uncertainty remains as we navigate end market complexities and a range of potential outcomes across several key regions. Our wider sales guidance ranges for both PPA and C&F reflect those complexities. In Production & Precision Ag, we expect net sales up between 5%-15%. This range reflects visible improvements to the North American Ag Equipment industry, though the ultimate magnitude of that improvement will depend on a number of factors, most of which have been volatile as of late.

Aging fleets and required replacement demand, coupled with declining used inventories, give the lower end of our sales outlook a very solid foundation. The upper end of our guidance range reflects a sustained finish to our combine Early Order Program and improving customer confidence throughout the year that carries into our rolling tractor order book. Conditions in Europe and in Brazil remain difficult, and there's greater uncertainty around when those two markets will turn. We believe Brazil could improve in 2027, given the current industry volumes at historic lows, combined with a rapidly aging fleet. At the same time, crop fundamentals, weather risk, and high interest rates will likely keep any improvement muted until the back half of 2027.

Moving to Construction & Forestry, we expect sales flat to up 10%. Construction end markets remain healthy, and our order books are strong, giving us good visibility into next year. The duration of demand tailwinds from data centers and other large non-residential projects is something we're watching closely, though most of that uncertainty is weighted towards 2028. Currently, dealer fleets remain below target levels, following a couple years of cumulative underproduction. This gives us room to improve those positions and build field inventory should confidence in end market outlooks continue to build. Our sales guide reflects strong near-term demand while maintaining flexibility on field inventory positioning as we monitor how demand develops heading into 2028.

Lastly, Small Ag & Turf is more balanced, with its diverse end markets and global footprint providing solid footing for next year. While we anticipate some downward industry pressure in Europe, we expect sales to be roughly flat, supported by continued strength across dairy, livestock, and turf markets.

Dan Pulley: Thank you both. Now we will cover a few topics before opening the line for questions. Let's start with our 2026 results. Chris, can you walk us through the fourth quarter, including how we finished the year relative to our guidance?

Christopher (Chris) Seibert: Sure, Dan. Happy to do that. The fourth quarter was a good example of the balance across our portfolio. Sales for Production & Precision Ag were down 15% on the quarter, as North American Large Ag demand stayed at low levels, and we kept production disciplined in South America. Conversely, Small Ag & Turf and Construction & Forestry grew 10% and 12% respectively on higher shipments and favorable price realization. This positioned overall Equip Ops sales to finish roughly flat for the quarter, with operating margins of 9.3%, reflecting disciplined spend management and strong execution to close out the year. All segments were in line or ahead of the guidance we gave last quarter.

For the full year, C&F sales rose nearly 22%, slightly ahead of our full-year outlook, following a strong fourth quarter finish. Infrastructure and non-residential construction, along with rental fleet replacement and growth, supported demand throughout the year. The 10.6% operating margin landed within our guide range, as favorable volumes and price realization throughout the year were partly offset by higher production costs and increased investments within SA&G and R&D tied to acquisitions and growth initiatives. Small Ag & Turf grew sales by roughly 15%, in line with our outlook, and delivered a 15.1% operating margin, reflecting strength across all regions, including a record year for our tractor business in India.

In Production & Precision Ag, full-year sales were down about 9%, reflecting industry declines across North America, South America, and Europe. Even at those demand levels, the segment delivered an 11.3% operating margin as we maintained production discipline, worked alongside our dealers to keep new inventories tight, reduced used inventory, and continued investing in the technology solutions our customers rely on.

T. Brent Norwood: Thanks, Chris. This is Brent. I want to emphasize how the business has changed through the cycle. Despite our largest business, PPA, operating in its second year at sub-trough levels, our Equip Ops as a whole delivered margin of more than 12%. This is more than 400 basis points higher than in 2016, when we were at a comparable point in the industry cycle, and nearly 700 basis points higher if we exclude tariffs. That performance reflects the structural changes we have made across the business: better cost management, tighter inventory discipline, and a growing share of revenue tied to high-value technologies.

Just as important, our earnings are far more diversified than they were a decade ago, when North American Large Ag mostly determined our financial results. This year, Construction & Forestry and Small Ag & Turf both grew by double digits while delivering strong profitability. For Production & Precision Ag, every region delivered double-digit margins despite challenging market conditions. That balance across segments and regions provides greater earnings stability and gives us the flexibility to continue investing for our customers through the cycle.

Dan Pulley: Thanks, Brent and Chris. Before we shift gears to 2027, let's discuss dealer inventory levels. Chris, can you help us understand where those stand today for North American Large Ag?

Christopher (Chris) Seibert: Sure, Dan. Our inventory of new Large Ag machines remains well-positioned and tight, down 10% from already low levels last year, with very few large combines and high-horsepower tractors across dealer lots. As we discussed in past quarters, we've prioritized managing used inventory since the downturn began, and the results clearly demonstrate those efforts. In North America, used high-horsepower tractor and combine inventories are both down double digits from a year ago. High-horsepower tractors are now down 25% from their peak, and used combines are down roughly 30%. More importantly, the quality of that inventory has improved as well.

The model year distribution of used combines is in line with our targets, and the mix of tractors has improved significantly, with model year 2023 and 2024 inventory down more than 40% from last year. Specifically, within this past quarter, we saw very strong activity in used combines, as year-end purchasing and harvest activity drove a double-digit reduction in inventory across our North American dealer network. We'll be watching for similar year-end purchasing activity in used tractors, which would further improve the setup for new tractor sales heading into the next growing season.

Dan Pulley: Thanks, Chris, for those details and the setup for demand next year. Let's shift to our outlook for agriculture and our order book positions as we enter the year. Can you walk us through the different regions?

Christopher (Chris) Seibert: Yeah. Let me start in North America, where we're seeing encouraging signs. In large tractors, order backlog momentum for fiscal year 2027 has grown steadily in recent weeks, and we now have orders in hand through the middle of the second quarter. Christopher (Chris) Seibert: Even with a tough year in Ag markets, technology adoption kept building. Engaged Acres are now over 530 million globally. However, globally, including Australia and Brazil, See & Spray covered approximately 12 million acres in 2026, delivering average herbicide savings of more than 50% across those acres. That momentum is continuing, with roughly one-third of orders in our recently concluded sprayer Early Order Program, including See & Spray. Moving to combines. Combines equipped with our Harvest Settings Automation technologies utilized the technology on more than double the acres this year, totaling to 11 million acres. John C. May: This is John, and I want to build on Chris's point about the scale of our data. #3063. Uber Riders Can Now Request to Have Their Trips Recorded

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

In four cities, Uber riders can request rides with drivers who use the Record My Ride feature.

Starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a new Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber says that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”

After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

Starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

Record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

“Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

Not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

“Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”

Uber says it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

Uber says it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.

#3062. Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026, plus more AI workplace updates

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The company also released new ROI tracking tools for companies monitoring their AI spend.

AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft said. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector

Microsoft said the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft said.

The company added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

Nadella also announced a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft said of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill

Microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can quickly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft announced a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the company’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise plans.

#3061. Anthropic’s Chip Choices Could Change the Nvidia Story. Here’s How.

Anthropic is spreading out its demand for AI accelerators across multiple companies.

By Chris Neiger – Nov 25, 2026 at 3:33PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›

Anthropic (ANT +1.08%) made headlines recently because of its blockbuster IPO, and investors are still trying to decide how the newly public artificial intelligence (AI) company will impact the broader AI market.

Some of the details Anthropic disclosed in its S-1 filing before going public shed light on its potential impact, especially on chip companies. Anthropic currently has deals with multiple chip companies to help provide the compute capacity it needs for its AI services.

Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) is, unsurprisingly, a key supplier of chips to Anthropic, but so are Alphabet (GOOGL -2.13%) (GOOG -2.02%), Amazon (AMZN -3.12%), and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -1.75%). Instead of tying itself to just one chip company, Anthropic has decided to spread out its chip vendors.

That could change Nvidia's growth narrative in the coming years. Here's how it's shifting and why Nvidia investors don't need to panic just yet.

Between cloud computing contracts and chip deals, Anthropic is on the hook for about $900 billion in spending over the next several years. That's a heck of a lot of money to spend, and Anthropic hopes it will accelerate its sales far beyond the company's current annual revenue run rate of $81 billion.

It's also far too much money to funnel toward just one or two AI infrastructure companies. To minimize its supply chain risks, ensure it has the most advanced technology, and negotiate better chip prices, Anthropic spreads its chip deals across four key players.

Here are Anthropic's biggest AI chip deals:

While Anthropic doesn't disclose all the details of each deal, including how much they might be worth, this data shows that Anthropic is clearly hedging its bets when it comes to buying AI chips.

Nvidia's GPUs are still among the most in-demand chips in the world, and they're very likely to remain so for years to come due to AI infrastructure spending. Nvidia had an estimated 80%-90% market share of AI accelerators last year and is estimated to have 75% this year.

That's both good and bad news for Nvidia. Having three-quarters of the AI accelerator market is huge, and it's part of the reason why Nvidia just reported another impressive quarter, with Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue rising 103% to $115.8 billion and earnings per share jumping 111% to $2.68.

But AMD's GPUs and custom silicon from Google, Broadcom, and Amazon are reducing Nvidia's dominance. Part of the reason is that custom chips (like the ones Anthropic buys from Nvidia rivals) are good at handling agentic AI tasks and are more efficient than the raw processing power from GPUs.

What's more, Nvidia's gross margins, while still high, are declining. The company said gross margins will be between 71% and 72% in the fourth quarter, down from nearly 75% in the third quarter. This downward pressure is mostly coming from rising memory costs right now, but intensifying chip competition could weigh on margins further in the coming years.

Still, while Nvidia shareholders should be aware of how rival chip companies could impact the company over time, Nvidia is still the leading AI accelerator company. Its recent revenue guidance for 75% growth in the fourth quarter -- up from its previous guidance of 70% -- should reassure investors that the company isn't getting sidelined anytime soon.

#3059. The Best Foldable Phones to Give This Holiday Season

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

For the tech enthusiast in your life, a foldable phone could be an interesting alternative to a traditional smartphone. We've rounded up our top picks, from book-style designs to flip phones.

If you’re shopping for someone this holiday season who deserves something a little more special — and you’ve got the budget to spare — a foldable phone can be a unique and practical gift that your loved one will use long after the holidays are over.

After reviewing our fair share of foldable phones, we’ve narrowed down our top three picks for the holidays and the perfect person on your list for each one. Who knows, you might end up caving in and treating yourself to a brand-new device? (You’ve been warned.)

For more mobile gift ideas, from budget-friendly smartphones to wearable devices, be sure to check out the video below.

The iPhone Duo is far from the first foldable phone, but as Apple’s debut into the market, it’s generated plenty of buzz. The Duo’s superpower is its ability to integrate hardware and software, creating a seamless experience across both displays.

The compact, 5.4-inch cover screen is great for sending texts and emails and checking notifications. The more expansive 7.6-inch inner display is ideal for multitasking, watching movies and working. It feels like using a smaller version of an iPad Mini that you can just fold up and toss in your pocket or bag.

The Duo is a great gift for someone who’s said they want a foldable phone, but refused to get one of the long-standing Android options already on the market. At last, Apple has its own offering that lets you stick with iOS. It’s a handy pick for people who often work on their phones and don’t always want to lug around a laptop. It’s also good for anyone who watches a lot of movies and TV shows on their mobile device. Plus, as a phone-tablet hybrid, it’s just fun to use.

The iPhone Duo isn’t perfect. It doesn’t support Face ID, but Apple did recently add an option to unlock the phone using the front camera. This isn’t as secure as Face ID, so you’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode for more sensitive functions like using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and after around 45 minutes of inactivity.

The Duo’s cameras also aren’t as advanced as what you’ll get with the iPhone 18 Pro models, which have larger main-camera sensors and more advanced optical zoom capabilities. There’s also no telephoto camera on the Duo. Still, most people will be happy with the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide rear cameras, as well as the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen. The FaceTime camera on the inner display is best suited for video calls rather than snapping quality photos.

Multitasking on the Duo is seamless, but it’s not as flexible as it is on other foldable phones. You can only have two apps open side by side, and you can’t readjust them.

Perhaps the biggest downside is the price. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage. That’s why it’s a good idea to keep an eye out for any deals that can help lower the price.

For the Android-lover in your life, there’s no better foldable pick than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Like the iPhone Duo, this phone has a passport-size design. (Technically, Samsung beat Apple to the punch, but let’s refrain from the “Who Did It First?” game for now.)

The Z Fold 8 has a 5.5-inch cover screen and a 7.6-inch inner display that’s great for watching videos, working and multitasking with up to three apps, which you can resize to your liking.

It’s also very thin, measuring 9.7mm thick when folded and 4.5mm thick when unfolded. That means it feels similar in thickness to a standard nonfolding phone, even when it’s closed. The Z Fold 8 fits squarely in a palm and easily slides into a pocket – tiny women’s pockets included.

Like the iPhone Duo, the Z Fold 8 doesn’t have a telephoto camera. But the 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras on the back and the 10-megapixel selfie cameras do a solid job.

The Z Fold 8 is also priced on the higher end, starting at $1,900 for 256GB. But its compact, sleek design and versatility help to make up for that sticker shock. Again, it’s a good idea to look out for any deals, especially around the holidays.

Some people prefer flip phones for their nostalgic designs and compact size. Motorola has plenty to choose from, but the best and most affordable pick for most people is the baseline 2026 Razr.

The phone features a classic clamshell design and a spacious 3.6-inch cover screen, making it easy to check notifications, reply to texts, control music or follow navigation without opening the phone. The 6.9-inch inner display feels like using an average nonfolding phone, even if the screen is a little narrower and taller.

For most people, the Razr’s 50-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras and 32-megapixel selfie camera on the inner display will do the trick. There’s no room for a telephoto camera, but the Razr pulls its weight for more casual photography.

The Razr’s processor isn’t as powerful as what you’ll get on the pricier Razr Plus and Razr Ultra, but as long as you’re not playing intensive games all day, you probably won’t notice the difference.

The Razr’s $800 starting price is significantly lower than the cost of book-style folding devices like the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. The Razr could be a more appealing option for someone who doesn’t need a phone-tablet hybrid but just wants a phone that’s fun to use and taps into the nostalgia of the original Motorola Razr.

No matter which phone you choose, your lucky recipient will enjoy the holiday spirit long after the season has passed, all while making quite the statement.

#3058. Microsoft’s new Licensed Weights lets businesses customize AI models with their own data

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Microsoft is bridging the gap between proprietary and open-weight AI while targeting data-conscious businesses.

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5

MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, said during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft said it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman said during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman said of the new coding model the company announced at Ignite.

The company also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

#3057. Coca-Cola Has Raised Its Dividend 64 Straight Years. Here's What $10,000 Will Pay You in 2027.

This Dividend King pays investors reliably, but its stock price has run ahead of the business.

By Neil Patel – Nov 25, 2026 at 3:47PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›

Investors can't help but think about the 2026 performance of a popular defensive name. The S&P 500, with heavy exposure to technology and artificial intelligence, is only up 6% this year (as of Nov. 23). Coca-Cola (KO -0.03%), on the other hand, has soared 37%.

The beverage stock isn't known for its growth potential, which has been a pleasant surprise in 2026. Instead, investors choose to buy and hold this industry-leading company because it's a safe choice that can generate a healthy dividend stream.

Coca-Cola has raised its dividend payout for a mind-blowing 64 straight years, making it a Dividend King, or a company that has raised its payout for 50 years or more. Purchasing $10,000 worth of its shares today will bring in this much passive income in 2027.

Coca-Cola's board of directors approved a roughly 4% dividend hike on Feb. 19. The quarterly payout climbed from $0.51 to $0.53 per share, or $2.12 annualized.

Today's annual payout is 51% higher than the $1.40 per share paid in 2016. That's about 4.2% annualized growth. It isn't spectacular. But it's consistent, surviving a pandemic and a bout of high inflation.

Here's the math investors care about. Buying $10,000 at the current share price of $95.88 gets you 104 shares. Based on today's payout, that position would generate more than $220 in dividend income in 2027. If the board delivers another raise in February, a near certain event, that figure will obviously be higher.

The dividend yield sits at 2.21%. The S&P 500 yields just 1.12%. Consequently, $10,000 in an S&P 500 index fund would produce only about $112 a year. Coca-Cola nearly doubles that.

There's a catch, though. Coca-Cola yielded 2.66% the day after its February raise. This stock's impressive rally this year has pushed the yield much lower. Income investors are now paying more for every dollar of dividends.

Nobody questions the quality of this business. Coca-Cola sells drinks in more than 200 countries and territories. Its flagship trademark is the world's most valuable food and beverage brand, according to Kantar.

That brand strength translates into durable pricing power. In the third quarter, net revenue grew 7% year over year to $13.4 billion. Unit case volume, a measure of how much product consumers bought, jumped 5%. Yet price/mix (higher prices plus a richer product mix) still added 1%. Coca-Cola sold more without sacrificing price.

Profitability improved. The comparable operating margin, which excludes one-time items, widened to 32.9% from 31.9%. Comparable earnings per share (EPS) rose 11% to $0.91, beating Wall Street's $0.88 estimate. Management now expects full-year comparable EPS growth of at least 11%.

Valuation is the problem. Coca-Cola trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 28.3. The S&P 500's index's P/E multiple is 20.3. That's a 39% premium for a company that isn't built for speed.

Management's long-term targets call for 4% to 5% organic revenue growth (excluding currency and acquisitions). Sell-side analysts expect the top line to shrink in 2027.

This year's gain was less about profits. The stock's 37% surge far outpaces that 11% earnings outlook for the year. Investors simply paid more for each dollar of earnings, with the P/E ratio rising 23% in 2026. That can't continue indefinitely.

I wouldn't buy Coca-Cola at today's price. With the best outcome being mid- to high-single-digit growth ahead, the valuation leaves little room for upside. Patient investors who appreciate the dividend should wait for a cheaper entry point.

#3054. Uber, Nuro and Lucid Begin Fully Driverless Testing With Their Luxury Robotaxi

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The Lucid Gravity robotaxi is one step closer to a commercial launch.

Nearly a year after showcasing their “luxurious” robotaxi at CES, Uber, Nuro and Lucid have started fully driverless testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, the companies said Tuesday.

The partnership, announced in July 2025, combines Uber’s ride-hailing platform, Nuro’s self-driving technology and Lucid’s electric vehicles. Autonomous rides take place aboard the Lucid Gravity robotaxi, which I had the opportunity to see first at a CES showcase in January (in the form of a “production intent design”), and then on the road this summer, with a safety driver behind the wheel.

Now, the partnership is ready to take its next big step, beginning with employee rides “soon,” the companies said. They plan to launch commercial robotaxi operations in the first quarter of 2027 in the San Francisco Bay Area, before expanding to Houston later next year. Lucid will begin manufacturing the first vehicles designed specifically for the commercial launch fleet “in the coming weeks.” Uber plans to deploy around 35,000 Lucid vehicles equipped with the Nuro Driver in the coming years in “dozens” of cities.

“Removing the safety operator from behind the wheel is an important milestone in our partnership with Nuro and Lucid, and a testament to all three partners’ focus on executing against our shared roadmap,” Samarth Kejriwal, Uber’s global head of autonomous mobility, said in a statement. “As we prepare for our first driverless passenger rides in the coming months, we’ll be working closely together to refine our operations, infrastructure and the in-cabin experience to ensure a safer, more comfortable ride.”

Nuro says it’s been conducting “round-the-clock autonomous testing of the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area and Houston” since December 2025, with a safety driver in the vehicle who can take over if needed.

In May, Nuro received a California Public Utilities Commission Drivered Pilot Permit, giving the company the green light to conduct pilot testing for an autonomous passenger service with a safety driver. Nuro also received a California Department of Motor Vehicles Driverless Testing Permit in April, allowing it to test self-driving vehicles without a safety driver.

Uber’s partnership with Nuro and Lucid is just one of dozens it has with other AV companies, including Waymo, Zoox, Avride, Wayve and May Mobility. Adding driverless options to an app that’s likely already on someone’s phone could increase their chances of giving the experience a try — despite the trepidation many people have about self-driving vehicles.

The Lucid Gravity robotaxi can seat up to six passengers, unlike rides from Waymo and Zoox that seat up to four. It has plenty of legroom and ample space for luggage in the back. The vehicle’s sensor suite is equipped with cameras, lidar sensors and radars for autonomous navigation.

It’s been a big year for autonomous vehicles, and it appears 2027 will be no different. The rapid expansion of AVs comes amid heightened scrutiny. Last week, the California DMV banned Waymo’s robotaxis from state freeways after a series of high-profile incidents — after which Waymo paused all of its freeway rides. Waymo, the largest player in the AV space, has been involved in a number of other safety incidents as it expands to more cities. Over the years, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has launched investigations into other AV companies, including Zoox and Tesla.

It’s against this landscape — and the full-speed-ahead race toward autonomy — that Nuro, Uber and Lucid will soon publicly debut their own robotaxi.

#3053. I’ve tested Ubuntu 27.04 ahead of its April release – and it will wow you

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

I've been using Ubuntu 27.04, and the speed boost is noticeable. Here's what else is coming.

Ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

This is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful
